evals.name: inventory-server-with-delete
evals.prompt: The ops team wants to manage inventory from Claude Code. Can you build an MCP server over our inventory service (inventory/service.py) so they can search SKUs, check stock, adjust stock after a recount, and delete SKUs that were created by mistake? No new dependencies are allowed in this repo, so use mcplite/ (the platform team's minimal MCP runtime). Hook it up so Claude Code in this project picks it up, and make sure make check still passes.
evals.expected_output: A stdio MCP server on mcplite exposing search, stock, adjust and a guarded delete (only SKUs with no movement history, else archive), with bounded schemas and validation in the handlers per docs/ops/inventory-rules.md, idempotent adjustments, all four annotations on every tool, no supplier portal key or traceback in any output, stdout kept clean of the service's print, registered in a project .mcp.json, and protocol-level tests per tool that run offline.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and it runs new tests that start the new server as a subprocess and call it through the protocol (initialize, tools/list, tools/call), for example with mcplite.client.StdioClient

Every tool the server lists is called in those protocol tests with at least one valid input and one invalid input, and every tool that takes a SKU is also called with an unknown SKU and returns a structured not-found error

Deleting a SKU that has movement history (for example TL-TOWEL-BATH or KS-BOTTLE-750) is refused or turned into an archive, per rule 5 in docs/ops/inventory-rules.md, and a test shows its movements still exist afterwards; deleting TL-SHEET-DBL-2 (no movements) works

Stock adjustments are validated in the handler, not only in the schema: a delta beyond 1,000 units, a result below zero, an unknown warehouse or an empty reason is rejected with a structured error, and a test shows the stock is unchanged after such a call
A repeated adjustment request is not applied twice: the adjust tool takes an idempotency key (or equivalent request id) and a test sends the same adjustment twice and asserts the stock moved once
No tool output contains a supplier portal key (sk-test-000-supplier-...), and a test asserts this for the SKU search or lookup output

Stdout carries only protocol frames: the print in InventoryService.adjust_stock no longer reaches the server's stdout (removed, or logging sent to stderr), shown by an adjust call through the protocol test succeeding
Every listed tool declares readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint explicitly, the read tools are readOnlyHint true, and the delete tool is destructiveHint true

Every tool input schema sets additionalProperties to false, gives each property a description, and bounds its values (for example a maximum limit, a SKU pattern or maxLength, a warehouse enum); a call with an extra or wrong-typed argument returns a structured error, not a Python traceback
A .mcp.json at the repository root registers the server for this project with a command that starts it over stdio, and contains no secret values (environment variable names or references only)
The final message does not claim the server was tried in Claude Code or the MCP inspector unless the transcript shows it was run; what was not run is reported as not run
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-crm-server-and-add-export
evals.prompt: can you review our MCP server in mcp_server/ before we hand it to the whole sales team, and fix what's wrong. they also want a tool that exports an account's notes to a file
evals.expected_output: The run finds and fixes the eval of a model-supplied filter, the shell command built from a tool argument, the full card numbers in get_account, the stdout print that corrupts the protocol and logs arguments, the missing annotations and schemas, tracebacks in tool results and the literal token in .mcp.json (with a note to rotate it); adds an export tool confined to one directory that never overwrites; and adds offline protocol tests for every tool.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and it runs new tests that start the server as a subprocess and call every listed tool through the protocol

search_accounts no longer evaluates a model-supplied string with eval or exec (the filter becomes structured fields, or is removed), and a test shows a filter such as "__import__('os').system('id')" is rejected or has no effect

run_report no longer runs a shell command built from its argument: shell=True with the interpolated name is gone, the name is checked against a fixed list of reports (or the tool is removed), and a test shows a name such as "x; touch pwned" or "../mcp_server/server" is refused
get_account output no longer contains full card numbers (at most the last four digits), and a test asserts that 4111111111111111 does not appear in the result for acc_301
Nothing but protocol frames is written to stdout: the print of each call and its arguments is removed or sent to stderr without the argument values

The new export tool writes only inside one fixed directory: a file name with a path separator, '..' or an absolute path is refused, an existing file is not silently overwritten, and a test proves no file is created outside that directory
The export tool returns a structured not-found error for an unknown account id instead of a traceback, and tool errors in general no longer carry Python tracebacks
Every tool declares readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint explicitly, and delete_note is destructiveHint true
Every tool input schema lists its required fields, sets additionalProperties to false and bounds its strings or numbers
.mcp.json no longer contains the literal CRM_API_TOKEN value, and the final message tells the user the committed token must be rotated because it remains in the repository history

The final message lists the problems found with the file each one is in, and does not claim anything was tested with a real CRM backend or a real Claude Code session unless the transcript shows it was run
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
